evidenceAudit.scope: Woman of reproductive age with pain or bleeding and a positive pregnancy test in the emergency department (ED): recognition, transvaginal ultrasound, human chorionic gonadotrophin (hCG) follow-up, expectant, medical (methotrexate) and surgical management, and anti-D immunoglobulin.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-18.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: NICE NG126 gives no methotrexate dose, route, contraindications or analgesic agents; the dose (50 mg/m² intramuscularly) is from one Australian hospital local operating procedure (2017, review overdue) and has not been compared with a Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists or Saudi guideline.
No Saudi Ministry of Health or Saudi Society of Obstetrics guideline was opened.
NICE NG126 advises anti-D immunoglobulin only after surgical management in rhesus-negative women; local policy in Saudi Arabia may differ.
Source pages were read through automated page extraction rather than page-by-page in the original documents, so each figure should be spot-checked against the source during clinical review.
The Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA) drug registration site could not be opened from this environment, so registration of each medicine was not verified; check hospital formulary.

pathophysiology.summary: A pregnancy implants outside the uterine cavity; NICE NG126 covers tubal ectopic pregnancy. Ectopic pregnancy can present with shoulder tip pain, collapse, tachycardia or hypotension, and moderate to large free fluid on scan may represent haemoperitoneum. About a third of women with ectopic pregnancy have no identifiable risk factors, so it must be excluded in anyone with symptoms. Serum hCG alone cannot locate the pregnancy; rise or fall over 48 hours guides follow-up.

clinicalManagement.title: Triage and stabilise
actions: Refer haemodynamically unstable women or those with significant pain or bleeding directly to the emergency department.
Do a pregnancy test in any woman of reproductive age with consistent symptoms.

clinicalManagement.title: Transvaginal ultrasound
actions: Locate the pregnancy; look for adnexal mass, fetal pole, heartbeat and free fluid.
If no pregnancy location is seen, repeat hCG at 48 hours and follow the rise or fall thresholds.

clinicalManagement.title: Choose management
actions: Expectant: repeat hCG on days 2, 4 and 7; if it falls by 15% or more, repeat weekly until under 20 IU/L.
Methotrexate: 50 mg/m² intramuscularly with hCG on days 4 and 7 then weekly.
Surgery: laparoscopic salpingectomy unless other infertility risk factors, in which case consider salpingotomy.

clinicalManagement.title: Anti-D immunoglobulin
actions: Offer 250 IU (50 micrograms) to rhesus-negative women having a surgical procedure; not for medical management alone.

clinicalManagement.title: Follow-up
actions: After salpingectomy: urine pregnancy test at 3 weeks. After salpingotomy: hCG at 7 days then weekly until negative.

regimens.indication: Medical management of unruptured tubal ectopic pregnancy
regimens.patientGroup: Women of reproductive age meeting local criteria (less than 8 weeks, mass under 4 cm, hCG under 5,000 units/L)
regimens.dose: 50 mg/m² of body surface area, capped at 2 m² (maximum 100 mg)
regimens.duration: One dose; consider a second dose or surgery if hCG does not fall by more than 15% between days 4 and 7
adjustments: Body surface area = square root of height in cm multiplied by weight in kg divided by 3600; capped at 2 m².
Treat only if liver function tests, urea and electrolytes and full blood count are normal; the source gives no other renal or hepatic adjustment.
Avoid pregnancy for 3 months; start oral contraception or use barrier contraception at the end of treatment.
monitoring: hCG on day 4; day 7 hCG, full blood count, urea and electrolytes and liver function tests; weekly until hCG is zero.
Review earlier if levels plateau or rise.
contraindications: Pain or tenderness, ruptured ectopic, haemodynamic instability, abnormal liver function tests, hCG at or above 5,000 units/L (local protocol), living far from the hospital or unable to attend follow-up.
Avoid NSAIDs (use paracetamol), folate supplements, sun exposure, alcohol, smoking and intercourse until resolved.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Clinically stable, pain free, mass under 35 mm, no visible heartbeat, hCG 1,000 IU/L or less, able to return.
No significant pain, unruptured, mass under 35 mm, no heartbeat, hCG under 1,500 IU/L, no intrauterine pregnancy, able to return.
Significant pain, mass 35 mm or larger, visible heartbeat, hCG 5,000 IU/L or more, or unable to return after methotrexate.

teaching.scope: Woman of reproductive age with pain or bleeding and a positive pregnancy test in the emergency department (ED): recognition, transvaginal ultrasound, human chorionic gonadotrophin (hCG) follow-up, expectant, medical (methotrexate) and surgical management, and anti-D immunoglobulin.
learningObjectives: Exclude ectopic in any woman with symptoms and a positive test.
Choose expectant, medical or surgical care by pain, mass size, heartbeat and hCG.
pitfalls: Missing ectopic because there are no risk factors.
Giving methotrexate to a woman who cannot return for follow-up.
keyPoints: Do not use hCG to locate the pregnancy.
A third of cases have no risk factors.
